name: GREEN — supported BPFI diagnosis
research_note: Phase 7B retained global 95% LAC as the candidate in-domain abstention mechanism. Across five in-domain splits, empirical coverage was about 95.64% and review about 4.36%; only two base errors were observed, so this is not a zero-error safety claim.

name: AMBER — ambiguous healthy vs impeller
research_note: A multi-class conformal set is treated as ambiguity rather than forced certainty. Phase 8A showed genuine multi-class sets on harder independent hydraulic tasks.

name: RED — severe sensor degradation
research_note: Phase 3C showed severe corruption can produce confidently wrong diagnoses. Under Gaussian 10 dB, balanced accuracy fell to about 0.345 while mean classifier confidence increased. Sensor health is therefore a separate hard gate.

name: RED — unsupported operating condition
research_note: Phase 4B showed that predictive OOD evidence confounds unknown faults with unseen operating speed. Predictive-entropy AUROC fell to about 0.660 and known unseen-speed false alarms were about 89.2%, so domain support must be checked first.

name: RED — novel / unknown fault evidence
research_note: Phase 4A found predictive entropy to be a strong held-fault OOD indicator inside represented operating conditions, with mean AUROC about 0.997. The final architecture still treats novelty evidence as an explicit gate rather than an autonomous diagnosis.

name: AMBER — weak independent valve classifier
dataset_context: UCI Condition Monitoring of Hydraulic Systems
research_note: Phase 8A valve-condition diagnosis was weak (mean balanced accuracy about 0.441). The 95% conformal layer routed about 99.52% of cases to review and produced mean set size about 3.48 rather than forcing one class.
